metadata.title: How to Use Seedance: Step-by-Step AI Video Guide
metadata.description: Learn how to use Seedance 2.0, choose a supported workflow, write a usable video prompt, and review the result before you publish.

hero.title: How to Use Seedance
hero.description: A Seedance 2.5 guide and Seedance 2.0 tutorial for accessing the current generator, choosing text-to-video, image-to-video, or video-to-video, and turning an idea into a checked export.
hero.tip: Availability, pricing, and supported settings can vary by provider, region, and plan.

introduce.title: A practical Seedance workflow
introduce.description: The fastest way to learn how to use Seedance is to separate creative decisions from generation settings. Start with one clear shot, then iterate with evidence from the preview.

items.title: Choose the right access point
items.description: Use the browser generator for the Seedance 2.0 workflows currently connected to Seadance Video. Seedance 2.5 access depends on a supported provider.

items.title: Describe one observable shot
items.description: State the subject, action, setting, camera movement, lighting, duration, and aspect ratio instead of combining unrelated ideas.

items.title: Add a reference only when useful
items.description: Use an image or source video to anchor identity, composition, or motion, then explain what should change and what must remain stable.

items.title: Review before publishing
items.description: Check motion, faces, text, audio, dimensions, watermark status, and rights before you download or share the result.

benefits.title: Pick a workflow that matches your goal
benefits.description: These paths cover the common Seedance 2.0 guide and access questions without promising capabilities that the selected provider does not expose.

items.title: Prompt-first generation
items.description: Use text-to-video when the scene is easier to direct in language than to anchor with an existing asset. Include timing and camera language.

items.title: Reference-guided generation
items.description: Use image-to-video when the first frame, product appearance, or character identity matters more than starting from a blank canvas.

items.title: Video-to-video iteration
items.description: Use a reference clip when motion or blocking is the starting point. Confirm that the selected model and provider support video input.

items.title: Credit-aware iteration
items.description: Review the estimated credit cost and choose a short draft before spending on a longer or higher-resolution output.

features.title: How to use Seedance step by step
features.description: A repeatable six-step process works for a Seedance tutorial, a social clip, a product concept, or a cinematic experiment.

items.title: 1. Define the shot
items.description: Write the subject, setting, action, camera, lighting, duration, and aspect ratio in plain language.

items.title: 2. Build the prompt
items.description: Use concrete verbs and sequence actions by time so the model has an unambiguous directing brief.

items.title: 3. Select the input mode
items.description: Choose text-to-video, image-to-video, or video-to-video according to the material you need to preserve.

items.title: 4. Run a short draft
items.description: Test framing, motion, identity, and audio before moving to a more expensive duration or resolution.

items.title: 5. Inspect the middle
items.description: Look beyond the opening frame for drifting hands, changing objects, flicker, broken text, or lip-sync problems.

items.title: 6. Export responsibly
items.description: Verify file dimensions, format, rights, and provider terms before commercial use or public distribution.

faq.title: How to Use Seedance FAQ
faq.description: Clear answers for the most common Seedance searches and workflows.

items.question: How to use Seedance 2.0 online?
items.answer: To access Seedance 2.0 online, open the generator, sign in when you are ready to submit, choose a supported mode, add your prompt or reference, review the estimate, and generate.

items.question: How to use Seedance 2.5?
items.answer: Seedance 2.5 is available through supported official consumer and API surfaces, but access varies by platform and region. This site currently connects its browser generator to Seedance 2.0.

items.question: How to use Seedance in offline mode?
items.answer: The browser workflow on this site requires an online connection. Official hosted providers and APIs also handle model execution remotely; do not assume an offline local model is available.

items.question: How to use Seedance 2.0 without being blocked?
items.answer: Read the provider message, remove unauthorized real-person or copyrighted references, and revise the request within the provider policy. Do not try to bypass moderation.

items.question: How do I make a Seedance video prompt better?
items.answer: Specify the subject, action, timing, camera, lighting, sound, and constraints. A short, testable shot is usually easier to improve than a prompt with many unrelated scenes.

cta.title: Start with a clear Seedance shot
cta.description: Use the current generator for a small test, then refine the prompt and settings with the review checklist.
